title: Arlo vs Wyze: Budget vs Premium Security Cameras
excerpt: Arlo sells premium weatherproof wireless cameras; Wyze sells budget cameras with local storage. Compare recording costs, detection, and ownership before buying.
body:
Arlo and Wyze anchor opposite ends of the camera market, and the decision between them is not really about which brand is better. It is about which trade-off you want: Wyze's subscription-free, local-storage simplicity or Arlo's polished, weatherproof wireless flexibility. Here is the head-to-head on the five things that actually decide it.

The storage model decides almost everything

Wyze cameras record to a microSD card with no mandatory subscription; the footage is yours, on hardware you own. Arlo cameras record to Arlo's cloud, with smart features behind the Arlo Smart plan. That single difference shapes everything else: cost over time, access away from home, and what happens if a company changes its plans. If no monthly fee is the priority, Wyze wins before you even compare specs, and our no-subscription camera guide lists more options in that camp.

Build quality and the great outdoors

Arlo's bodies are weather-sealed, built for porches and driveways, and designed to sit outside through rain and heat. Wyze's lineup skews indoor; some models carry weather ratings, but the budget design philosophy is a sheltered mount, not an all-weather sentinel. For front doors and garages, Arlo tolerates conditions Wyze should not be asked to handle, and its magnetic mounts survive constant repositioning.

Detection: what each brand actually notices

Both brands offer motion zones and person detection, and both put deeper AI features — package detection, animal detection, familiar-face alerts — behind subscriptions. The difference is polish. Arlo's detection tuning and alert timeline are more refined; Wyze's are functional and free at the basic level. For a first camera on a budget, Wyze's detection is adequate. For a front-door camera where false alarms cost you sleep, Arlo's tuning matters more than its lens.

Video quality: 1080p versus 4K, honestly

Wyze delivers 1080p-class footage that is fine at close range: a room, a hallway, a pet. Arlo's 4K models add zoom-and-crop headroom for driveways and long approaches. Our resolution explainer walks through the mechanics. Indoors, you will struggle to tell the difference on a phone screen; outdoors at distance, you can.

Total cost of ownership, year one

Wyze's math is camera plus card, then nothing. Arlo's math is camera plus subscription to record, plus an optional solar panel for battery life. Over a year, the subscription often outweighs the hardware difference, which is why budget buyers and long-term planners lean Wyze, while premium buyers who value the app, weatherproofing, and zoom pay for Arlo. Neither is wrong; they optimize for different owners. And when you add a second or third camera, the math diverges further: each Wyze camera adds only hardware, while each Arlo camera shares the same cloud plan or pushes you toward a higher tier — check how the plan scales before you multiply cameras.

What happens to footage when the camera disappears

This is the scenario buyers skip and burglars do not. A Wyze camera recording to a microSD card keeps footage on the device, which means a stolen camera takes its evidence with it unless clips were backed up off-device. An Arlo camera recording to the cloud keeps the clip even if the camera is ripped off the wall. If theft of the camera itself is part of your threat model — an exposed porch, a shared hallway — cloud storage is not a luxury, it is the footage surviving. If the camera watches a nursery or a pet indoors, the risk barely registers and local storage wins on simplicity.

Who each camera is actually for

Choose Arlo when

  • The camera lives outside and faces real weather.
  • You want 4K zoom detail for identification after an event.
  • You accept a subscription for cloud clips and smart detection.

Choose Wyze when

  • You want local storage with no monthly fee, ever.
  • The camera watches an indoor room, nursery, or pet area.
  • You are buying a first camera or a multi-room set on a tight budget.

Bottom line: a monthly fee for polish, or a memory card for freedom

Pick Wyze for storage freedom and low running costs; pick Arlo for outdoor build, zoom detail, and a refined app. Avoid the trap of comparing spec sheets: compare the subscription, the mounting spot, and how you will actually review footage. Our common-mistakes guide covers the rest of the decision.
